solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Writer’s second copy — and editor’s first (6)

indicatorNotes.first: the editor's first letter is the E that opens 'editor'

blocks.note: s is the standard abbreviation for second
to crib is to copy someone else's work
first letter of 'editor'

annotation.surface: A writer handing over a second draft, with the editor taking first look.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Writer' works as 'is': the writer is what the rest of the clue builds.
annotation.definitionFit: A scribe is someone who writes, originally a copyist of documents.

entries.clue: Type of curdled milk, pint-sized with no top to swiftly go high (9)

indicatorNotes.with no top: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, so POCKET loses its P

blocks.note: skyr is an Icelandic cultured dairy product, like thick yoghurt
pint-sized = POCKET (as in pocket-sized), minus its first letter

annotation.surface: A recipe note about a tiny pot of soured milk rising fast.
annotation.walkthrough: SKYR is rare in English but turns up in crosswords; 'pint-sized' stands for POCKET as in a pocket edition.
annotation.definitionFit: To skyrocket is to rise very quickly, like a firework.

entries.clue: Salad course dressed with caviar? (7)

indicatorNotes.dressed with: the course is clothed by the caviar, which wraps around it

blocks.note: caviar is fish roe; it wraps the course
the main course of a meal

annotation.surface: A fancy salad served with caviar as a dressing.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface serves caviar as a dressing on a salad; in the wordplay the caviar is the dressing on the course, wrapped around it like clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: Romaine is cos lettuce, the classic salad leaf.

entries.clue: One outlawed and forbade the thing, reportedly (6)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is heard, so the letters follow the sound

blocks.note: forbade = banned, the thing = it

annotation.surface: A tale of an outlaw who banned something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banned it' said quickly is 'bandit', and a bandit is exactly someone outlawed.
annotation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber, historically an outlaw.

entries.clue: A support actor of dubious quality who almost died in the theatre? (7)

annotation.definition: who almost died in the theatre?

blocks.note: as written
a bra is a supporting undergarment
a ham is an over-acting performer

annotation.surface: A bad actor who nearly dies on stage.
annotation.walkthrough: Abraham Lincoln was shot in Ford's Theatre but died next morning in a house across the street, so he only 'almost' died in the theatre. The question mark flags the whimsy.
annotation.definitionFit: Abraham Lincoln was shot at Ford's Theatre and carried out before he died.

entries.clue: More than enough taste without the topping of salt (5)

indicatorNotes.without: 'without' means lacking, so the taste is served lacking the salt's letter
indicatorNotes.topping of: in a down clue the topping is the first letter, S of 'salt'

blocks.note: a taste of food is a sample
first letter of 'salt', removed

annotation.surface: A dish that has plenty of flavour even without salt sprinkled on top.
annotation.walkthrough: SAMPLE minus S leaves AMPLE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an ample helping is a generous one, with some to spare.

entries.clue: Florrie’s lingerie’s not entirely white (8)

indicatorNotes.not entirely: only part of the phrase is used, so the answer sits inside it

blocks.note: florRIE'S LINGerie

annotation.surface: Someone noting that Florrie's underwear is not pure white.
annotation.walkthrough: 'White' here is white wine, not a colour; Riesling is a German grape and its wine.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: in a wine list 'a white' is any white wine, and Riesling is a grape made into one.

entries.clue: Hot wearing suit in heated areas? (7)

indicatorNotes.wearing: the suit is worn around H, so it goes outside

blocks.note: hearts is one of the four card suits
h = hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Someone sweltering in a suit in a heated room.
annotation.walkthrough: HEART(H)S: the H slips in before the final S. The question mark admits a hearth is a fireplace floor rather than a whole heated area.
annotation.definitionFit: A hearth is the floor of a fireplace, where the heat is.

entries.clue: Small donation securing Republican headgear (5)

indicatorNotes.securing: the donation holds the R inside it

blocks.note: the widow's mite, a tiny gift in the Bible
r = Republican

annotation.surface: A small political donation buying a Republican hat.
annotation.walkthrough: The widow's mite is the Gospel story of a poor widow giving two tiny coins, so a mite is any small contribution.
annotation.definitionFit: A mitre is a bishop's tall pointed hat.

entries.clue: Disdainful of pork pie right after wine (8)

indicatorNotes.after: the pork pie and R are placed after the wine

blocks.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
Cockney rhyming slang: pork pie = lie
r = right

annotation.surface: A snooty diner turning up their nose at a pork pie served after the wine.
annotation.walkthrough: In British rhyming slang a pork pie (or 'porky') is a lie. A pork pie itself is a cold meat pie.
annotation.definitionFit: A cavalier attitude is offhand and dismissive.

entries.clue: Country address offered to chaps in the past? (5)

blocks.note: ye is the old way to address a group as 'you', as 'in the past' hints
chaps = men
tells you the form of address is an old one

annotation.surface: Wondering how a gathering of men used to be addressed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ye men!' is how an old speaker might hail a group of chaps; 'address' here is a form of words, not a postal address.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the answer is one particular country, on the southern tip of the Arabian peninsula.

entries.clue: Little programme skill in item on Bake Off? (5,4)

blocks.note: an applet is a small computer program
art = skill, as in the art of persuasion

annotation.surface: A small TV show about baking skills.
annotation.walkthrough: The Great British Bake Off is a TV baking contest. 'Programme' suggests television, but here it is software: APPLET.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: fruit pastries are a staple of the show's challenges.

entries.clue: Begin travelling to Nigeria (9)

indicatorNotes.travelling: things that travel do not stay put, so the letters move to new places

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A journey to Nigeria is about to start.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'to' belongs to the fodder, not a link.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the intransitive sense: where a river begins is where it originates.

entries.clue: Departed, grabbing time for coffee (5)

indicatorNotes.grabbing: LATE takes hold of T, so T goes inside

blocks.note: the late = the departed, the dead
t = time

annotation.surface: Someone leaving and grabbing time for a coffee on the way.
annotation.walkthrough: LAT(T)E. 'Departed' reads as 'left', but here it means dead, as in 'the late king'.
annotation.definitionFit: A latte is espresso with steamed milk.

entries.clue: Appreciated place with gardens around November (4)

indicatorNotes.around: the place goes around the November letter

blocks.note: Kew in west London, home of the Royal Botanic Gardens
N is November in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone enjoying a garden visit in November.
annotation.walkthrough: K(N)EW. Kew Gardens is London's great botanic garden.
annotation.definitionFit: To appreciate something can mean to know or understand it.

entries.clue: Eton’s involved in appealing fraud (10)

indicatorNotes.involved: involved means tangled up, so the letters of ETONS are mixed
indicatorNotes.in: the mixed letters go inside DISHY

blocks.note: dishy is British slang for attractive
ETONS mixed up

annotation.surface: Eton College caught up in an eye-catching scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: DISH(ONEST)Y. Eton is the famous English private school, and the 's supplies the S the fodder needs.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fraud is deceit for gain, the abstract quality being dishonesty.

entries.clue: Duck and hawk accepted by mostly fit place for treatment (8)

indicatorNotes.accepted by: the duck and hawk are taken inside the other word
indicatorNotes.mostly: most but not all of the word is used, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: fit = HALE, mostly so without its E; it wraps the rest
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
to hawk is to clear the throat and spit

annotation.surface: Two birds taken in by a place that nurses them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck and hawk' look like two birds but neither is: a duck is a cricket score of nought, and to hawk is to cough up.
annotation.definitionFit: A hospital is where patients are treated.

entries.clue: Rory hikes rocky Dales location (9)

indicatorNotes.rocky: unsteady, so the letters wobble into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Rory walking over rough ground in the Dales.
annotation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Dales are a hilly national park in northern England; 'rocky' fits the hike and scrambles the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by location: the Dales are a range of valleys that lie within this northern English county.

entries.clue: Piece of timber, to name something that floats in water (8)

blocks.note: a plank is a length of wood
as written
n = name

annotation.surface: Naming a piece of wood that floats.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the plank itself floats; the floater is the answer as a whole.
annotation.definitionFit: Plankton are tiny organisms drifting in the sea.

entries.clue: Chance of new start in Forbidden City when a king returned (6,4)

indicatorNotes.returned: sent back, so AS A R turns round

blocks.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo
LA = Los Angeles
as = when, as in 'as I left'
as written
r = rex, king

annotation.surface: A king coming back to Beijing's Forbidden City for a fresh start.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Forbidden City' wants to be Beijing's imperial palace; split in two, each word does its own job.
annotation.definitionFit: A tabula rasa, a blank slate, is the chance to start afresh.

entries.clue: Dwarf British tree not completely well-rounded (7)

blocks.note: b = British
the ash tree
well-rounded = FULL, not completely so without its last L

annotation.surface: A stunted British tree that has not quite filled out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dwarf' looks like a verb or an adjective for a small tree; it is a noun, one of Snow White's seven dwarfs.
annotation.definitionFit: Bashful is one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White.

entries.clue: Reject shortened branch railway (4)

indicatorNotes.shortened: a shortened word is cut at its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a synonym for reject, as in turning down an offer with scorn; 'shortened' cuts its final N

annotation.surface: A rail company cutting back an unwanted branch line.
annotation.walkthrough: SPURN minus its N.
annotation.definitionFit: A spur is a short branch line off a main railway.

entries.clue: Extend a number in Gershwin’s opening scene (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the number goes inside the scene

blocks.note: the American spelling of prologue, fitting the American Gershwin
n stands for a number in algebra

annotation.surface: Lengthening the start of a Gershwin show by adding a song.
annotation.walkthrough: PROLO(N)G. 'Number' suggests a song, but it is N; Gershwin signals the US spelling PROLOG.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to make something last longer, as in extending or prolonging a stay.

entries.clue: Window key earlier failing to open (6)

indicatorNotes.failing to open: the word loses its opening letter F

blocks.note: D is a musical key
earlier = FORMER, without its first letter

annotation.surface: A window whose key used to jam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' and 'failing to open' paint a stuck window lock, but the key is musical.
annotation.definitionFit: A dormer is a window projecting from a sloping roof.

entries.clue: Cell breaker only Sing Sing keeps locked up (5)

indicatorNotes.keeps locked up: the words hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: onLY SINg

annotation.surface: A jailbreak that Sing Sing prison keeps a lid on.
annotation.walkthrough: Sing Sing is a New York prison, so 'cell breaker' looks like an escapee; it is a biological cell.
annotation.definitionFit: A lysin is an antibody or enzyme that destroys cells.

entries.clue: London Met initially introducing old copper’s stand-in (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letters of London Met
indicatorNotes.introducing: L and M take the other letters in between

blocks.note: first letters of London and Met, split around the rest
o = old
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

annotation.surface: A police force bringing in a retired officer as cover.
annotation.walkthrough: L(OCU)M. The Met is London's police force, so 'copper' reads as a police officer, but it is the metal.
annotation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric standing in for another.

entries.clue: Silly fool messed around with virus (9)

indicatorNotes.messed around with: the letters of fool are jumbled together with virus

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: An idiot playing carelessly with a virus.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Silly fool' looks like one phrase; 'Silly' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a frivolous remark is a silly, lightweight one.

entries.clue: Make for church (5)

blocks.note: as written
CE = Church of England

annotation.surface: Heading off to church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Make for' reads as 'head towards'; split it and 'Make' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the compelling sense: 'they made me go' means they compelled me.

entries.clue: Celebrate in cold air in restaurant (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the celebration goes inside the cold air

blocks.note: c = cold, as on a tap
an air is a tune, as is an aria
to fete is to celebrate

annotation.surface: A party held in a chilly dining room.
annotation.walkthrough: C + A(FETE)RIA. 'Air' reads as breath or wind but is a tune.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific kind for the general: a cafeteria is the self-service sort of eatery.

entries.clue: Speech from revolutionary core of Africa (5)

indicatorNotes.core of: the middle of the word is taken

blocks.note: Mao Zedong, China's revolutionary leader
the middle two letters of afRIca

annotation.surface: A revolutionary making a speech in the heart of Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Speech' means a language: Maori is spoken in New Zealand, nowhere near Africa.
annotation.definitionFit: Maori is the language of New Zealand's indigenous people.

entries.clue: Confusion of language between Middle English and English (7)

indicatorNotes.between: the language sits between ME and E

blocks.note: ME = Middle English
lang is the abbreviation for language
e = English

annotation.surface: A muddle of languages caught between old and modern English.
annotation.walkthrough: ME + LANG + E.
annotation.definitionFit: A mélange is a jumbled mixture.

entries.clue: Black sharper footwear (6)

blocks.note: b = black, as on pencils
a sharper is a cheat or swindler, a rogue

annotation.surface: Smarter black shoes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sharper' looks like a comparative adjective, 'smarter'; it is a noun meaning a cardsharp or con man.
annotation.definitionFit: A brogue is a sturdy leather shoe with decorative perforations.
